from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Growth Analogy: From Scalars to Matrices", 
            [
                'Simple growth follows the equation dx/dt equals rx.', 
                'The solution is the familiar exponential function, e to rt.', 
                'In systems, matrices replace scalars to describe multi-variable growth.'
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Initial state: Line 1 highlighted
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        eq1 = Text("dx/dt = rx", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        # Start in the middle of the visual area
        self.place_in_area(eq1, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF")
        )
        
        # Solution equation
        eq2 = Text("x(t) = x(0)e^(rt)", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # Growth circle
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        # Position circle in the lower-left grid area
        self.place_in_area(circle, "D2", "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Move eq1 to top-left of the grid area and transform it into eq2
        self.play(
            Transform(eq1, self.place_at_grid(eq2, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)),
            Create(circle)
        )
        
        # Animate scalar growth (Circle scaling)
        self.play(circle.animate.scale(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight matrix concept line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        
        # Matrix equation on the right side of the grid
        eq3 = Text("dx/dt = Ax", font_size=32, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(eq3, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Coordinate system on the bottom right
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Basis vectors
        v1 = Vector([1, 0], color="#FF0000")
        v2 = Vector([0, 1], color="#00FF00")
        plane.add(v1, v2)
        
        # Dots for tracing paths
        dot1 = Dot(v1.get_end(), radius=0).set_opacity(0)
        dot2 = Dot(v2.get_end(), radius=0).set_opacity(0)
        plane.add(dot1, dot2)
        
        # Traced paths
        path1 = TracedPath(dot1.get_center, stroke_color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        path2 = TracedPath(dot2.get_center, stroke_color="#00FF00", stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(
            Write(eq3),
            Create(plane)
        )
        self.add(path1, path2)
        
        # Matrix transformation over time
        t_final = 1.2
        val = 0.2 * t_final
        rot = 0.7 * t_final
        # Final transformation matrix
        mat_final = np.exp(val) * np.array([
            [np.cos(rot), -np.sin(rot)],
            [np.sin(rot), np.cos(rot)]
        ])
        
        # Animate the linear transformation over time
        self.play(
            ApplyMatrix(mat_final, plane),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Matrix Exponentials: The Secret to System Evolution"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Definition of Matrix Exponential",
            "- Power Series Expansion",
            "- Solving Linear Systems",
            "- Transformation over Time",
            "- Decoupling via Eigenvalues"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Visualization of the Taylor Series for Matrix Exponential
        # Replacing MathTex with MarkupText to avoid the LaTeX dependency error
        formula = MarkupText(
            'e<sup>At</sup> = Σ<sub>k=0</sub><sup>∞</sup> (At)<sup>k</sup> / k!',
            color=YELLOW,
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=0.9)

        expansion = MarkupText(
            '= I + At + (At)<sup>2</sup> / 2! + ...',
            color=BLUE,
            font_size=28
        )
        self.place_at_grid(expansion, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Animations
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(expansion, shift=DOWN))
        self.wait(2)

        # Illustrate a simple 2x2 matrix evolution concept using Text and VGroup to avoid LaTeX
        m_a = Text("a", font_size=24)
        m_b = Text("b", font_size=24)
        m_c = Text("c", font_size=24)
        m_d = Text("d", font_size=24)
        m_grid = VGroup(m_a, m_b, m_c, m_d).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.4)
        m_lb = Text("[", font_size=44).next_to(m_grid, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        m_rb = Text("]", font_size=44).next_to(m_grid, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        matrix_example = VGroup(m_grid, m_lb, m_rb)
        
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_example, "F2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        vector_x = MarkupText("x(t) = e<sup>At</sup> x(0)", font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_x, "F5", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Create(matrix_example))
        self.play(Write(vector_x))
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup initial layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'The matrix exponential e^At is a power series.',
            'Identity plus At plus higher-order matrix powers.',
            "Time 't' scales the evolution of the system.",
            'Matrix powers warp the space over time.',
            'This transforms initial states into future trajectories.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Formal Definition of e^At", lecture_lines)

        # Matrix for evolution: A = [[0.2, -1.5], [1.5, 0.2]] (Spiral expansion)
        def get_matrix_at_t(t):
            exp_factor = np.exp(0.2 * t)
            angle = 1.5 * t
            cos_a = np.cos(angle)
            sin_a = np.sin(angle)
            return exp_factor * np.array([
                [cos_a, -sin_a, 0],
                [sin_a,  cos_a, 0],
                [0,      0,      1]
            ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid dependence on 'latex' binary
        formula = Text("e^At = sum (At)^k / k!", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text
        formula_expanded = Text("= I + At + (At)^2 / 2! + ...", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(formula_expanded, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_expanded, shift=DOWN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Slider UI
        slider_line = Line(self.grid["F2"], self.grid["F5"], color=WHITE)
        slider_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        slider_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            slider_line.point_from_proportion(t_tracker.get_value() / 2.0)
        ))
        # Replaced MathTex with Text
        t_label = Text("t = ", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        t_value = DecimalNumber(0, color=YELLOW, font_size=24, num_decimal_places=2, mob_class=Text)
        t_value.add_updater(lambda v: v.set_value(t_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.place_at_grid(t_label, "F1", scale_factor=1.0)
        t_value.next_to(t_label, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.add(slider_line, slider_dot, t_label, t_value)
        self.play(Create(slider_line), FadeIn(slider_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        
        # Coordinate Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C1", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Basis Vectors
        i_vec = Vector([1, 0], color=RED)
        j_vec = Vector([0, 1], color=GREEN)
        
        # Add Updaters for vectors
        def update_i(v):
            mat = get_matrix_at_t(t_tracker.get_value())
            new_end = mat @ np.array([1, 0, 0])
            v.put_start_and_end_on(plane.get_origin(), plane.c2p(new_end[0], new_end[1]))

        def update_j(v):
            mat = get_matrix_at_t(t_tracker.get_value())
            new_end = mat @ np.array([0, 1, 0])
            v.put_start_and_end_on(plane.get_origin(), plane.c2p(new_end[0], new_end[1]))

        i_vec.add_updater(update_i)
        j_vec.add_updater(update_j)
        
        # Trails
        i_trail = TracedPath(i_vec.get_end, stroke_color=RED, stroke_width=2)
        j_trail = TracedPath(j_vec.get_end, stroke_color=GREEN, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.add(plane, i_vec, j_vec, i_trail, j_trail)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Indicate(self.lecture[4]))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)

        # Define animation grid (Rows A-F, Cols 1-6) on the right half of the screen
        self.grid_coords = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        # Starting reference for the grid (center-right area)
        start_x = 1.0
        start_y = 2.0
        step = 0.9

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x_pos = start_x + (j * step)
                y_pos = start_y - (i * step)
                self.grid_coords[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_pos, y_pos, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos):
        """Helper to move mobjects to predefined grid alphanumeric keys."""
        if grid_pos in self.grid_coords:

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup()
        for line in lecture_lines:
            text = Text(line, font_size=20, color=WHITE)
            lecture_vgroup.add(text)
        
        self.lecture = lecture_vgroup.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Grid System for right side (Visual Area)
        self.grid = {}
        # Mapping rows A-F and cols 1-6 to coordinate space
        for i, row in enumerate(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]):
            for j, col in enumerate(["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.1 
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        lecture_points = [
            "- Matrix Exponential: e^At",
            "- Defined by Taylor Series",
            "- Solves dx/dt = Ax",
            "- Fundamental in Linear Systems",
            "- Maps time to state transitions"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Matrix Exponentials: System Evolution", lecture_points)
        
        # 2. Animation: Lecture Points Appearance
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(
                *[Write(line) for line in self.lecture],
                lag_ratio=0.5
            ),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Visual Element: The Taylor Series Formula
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        formula = Text(
            "e^At = I + At + (At)^2 / 2! + ...",
            font_size=28,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Visual Element: State Evolution Matrix
        # Manually constructing matrix to avoid Matrix class (which requires LaTeX)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with specific title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: Solving Linear Systems", 
            [
                'Systems of linear differential equations use this tool.', 
                'The solution is e to At times the initial state.', 
                'Matrix exponentials are the fundamental propagators of linear systems.'
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency errors
        diff_eq = Text("dx/dt = Ax", font_size=32)
        initial_cond = Text("x(0)", color="#FFA500", font_size=28)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(diff_eq, "A2", "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(initial_cond, "A5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(diff_eq), FadeIn(initial_cond))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Create solution text using VGroup to allow targeted coloring/animation of specific parts
        sol_eq = VGroup(
            Text("x(t) = ", font_size=32),
            Text("e^At", font_size=32),
            Text(" x(0)", font_size=32)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(sol_eq, "C2", "D5")
        
        # Create propagator label
        propagator_label = Text("Propagator", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(propagator_label, "D3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sol_eq))
        
        # Flash the term e^At and show label
        self.play(
            sol_eq[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            Indicate(sol_eq[1], color="#00FF00"),
            Write(propagator_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Define a vector field for the streamlines (stable spiral)
        def flow_func(p):
            x, y = p[:2]
            # Simple spiral sink dx/dt = -0.5x + y; dy/dt = -x - 0.5y
            return np.array([-0.5 * x + y, -x - 0.5 * y, 0])

        # Create StreamLines object
        stream_lines = StreamLines(
            flow_func, 
            x_range=[-2, 2], 
            y_range=[-2, 2], 
            stroke_width=2, 
            color=BLUE_E,
            opacity=0.4
        )
        self.place_in_area(stream_lines, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Add 5 dots to follow streamlines
        start_points = [
            [1.5, 1.5, 0], 
            [-1.5, 1.0, 0], 
            [1.0, -1.5, 0], 
            [-1.2, -1.2, 0], 
            [0.5, 1.8, 0]
        ]
        
        dots = VGroup()
        for pt in start_points:
            dot = Dot(point=pt, color="#00FFFF", radius=0.06)
            dots.add(dot)
        
        # Scale and move dots group relative to stream_lines
        dots.scale(0.6)
        dots.move_to(stream_lines.get_center())
        
        def update_dot(mob, dt):
            # Calculate direction relative to center of field
            relative_pos = (mob.get_center() - stream_lines.get_center()) / 0.6
            v = flow_func(relative_pos)
            mob.shift(v * dt * 0.4) 
            # Recycle dots if they get too close to center
            if np.linalg.norm(relative_pos) < 0.1:
                mob.move_to(stream_lines.get_center() + np.array([np.random.uniform(-1,1), np.random.uniform(-1,1), 0]))

        self.play(FadeIn(stream_lines))
        self.add(dots)
        
        # Attach updaters
        for dot in dots:
            dot.add_updater(update_dot)
            
        self.wait(4)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        for dot in dots:
            dot.remove_updater(update_dot)

        # Final state color correction
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Matrix Exponentials: The Secret to System Evolution
outline.target_audience: University students in Linear Algebra or Differential Equations

sections.title: The Growth Analogy: From Scalars to Matrices
sections.content: Start with the familiar scalar growth equation dx/dt = rx, where the solution is x(t) = e^(rt). Introduce the concept of extending this to systems of variables represented by vectors. Use a split-screen animation showing a single 'growing' circle (scalar) next to a 'stretching and rotating' grid (matrix).
sections.example: A single colony of bacteria growing at a rate 'r' versus a complex ecosystem of two interacting species (predators and prey) whose populations depend on each other through a matrix 'A'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Taylor Series Bridge
sections.content: Briefly revisit the Taylor Series for e^x. Explain that because we can add and multiply square matrices, we can plug a matrix into this power series. Visually show the summation terms 1 + x + x^2/2! + ... transforming into I + At + (At)^2/2! + ... with matrices visually stacking to form the final result.
sections.example: An animated 'Taylor Machine' where you feed in a scalar value to get a curve, then swap the input for a 2x2 matrix to see the components of the matrix evolve.

sections.title: The Formal Definition of e^(At)
sections.content: Define the matrix exponential e^(At) using the power series. Emphasize that 't' acts as a time scaling factor. Use a graphical representation of a coordinate plane where the basis vectors start to 'flow' along paths determined by the sum of these matrix powers.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Time-Travel Remote' where the button 't' smoothly warps a square grid into a skewed or rotated shape based on the instructions inside matrix A.

sections.title: The Computational Shortcut: Diagonalization
sections.content: Introduce the 'shortcut' for calculating e^(At) when matrix A is diagonalizable (A = PDP^-1). Explain that e^(At) = P * e^(Dt) * P^-1. Graphically show the process: 1. Change basis (P^-1), 2. Scale along axes (e^Dt), 3. Change back (P).
sections.example: A 'Robot Arm' (P) that re-orients a package so a simple 'Stretching Machine' (e^Dt) can work on it, before the arm rotates it back to the original orientation.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: Rotations and Scaling
sections.content: Show what different types of matrices produce in the exponential. A skew-symmetric matrix leads to a rotation (e^At is an orthogonal matrix), while a diagonal matrix leads to pure scaling. Use an animation of a character 'Vector' traveling in circles or spiraling outward.
sections.example: A compass needle (Vector) spinning in a magnetic field represented by a skew-symmetric matrix, showing continuous rotation as time 't' advances.

sections.title: Application: Solving Linear Systems
sections.content: Connect the math to the ultimate goal: solving the differential equation dx/dt = Ax. The solution is x(t) = e^(At) * x(0). Highlight that the matrix exponential is the 'fundamental solution' that transitions the system from the initial state to any future state.
sections.example: A flight simulator where the joystick input (matrix A) determines how the plane's orientation (x) evolves over time (t) starting from a takeoff position (x0).
